beers.name: Good Times

Some days are naturally gonna be better than others, and some don't go as planned, but as they say, you can turn lemons into lemonade. When it's time to pass up a beer, we respect that. beers.notes: Reissued. Welcome back to the third jam session in our ongoing series, featuring a trio of wicked berries. This session started with a creamy kettle-soured base that's been fermented really clean. Then we kept hitting it layers of hand-selected fruits until we reached the pitch-perfect harmony of tart, sweet, creamy and refreshing. Store chilled for the freshest performance.

beers.name: Happy Place
beers.notes: This is the quintessential brewer's beer. A classic style that is uncomplicated and easy to drink, but the exact opposite when it comes to the brewing. Endless careful practice, recipe crafting and flawless production technique are all that is needed to produce a full-flavoured and well-balanced Helles. Something that would make a proud Bavarian as happy to drink it as we are happy making it.

beers.name: Hang Time (Rocky Ridge Collab)
beers.notes: After making one delicious beer with our mates over in WA, the thirsty world demanded another. This time they came to us for a brew day, and we have created another classic for those demanding dry mouths. Hang time is a punchy, full-bodied hazy using the goodness of 2 hops we have never used before in NZ 101 and Alora. This NZ/US combo delivers passion and stone fruit to the moon that is backed up with tingly yuzu and lime zest and some sweet melon smooches.

beers.name: You Can Call Me Al (Aliment Collab)
beers.notes: Hi, my name is Al. I am the very special progeny of a collaboration between breweries Altitude and Aliment. I would like to tell you a bit about myself. I am beautiful dark bronze, fresh espresso colour with a soft tan foam on top. First impressions aside, you should smell my delicious top notes of baked rye sourdough, toasted caramel nuts, sticky toffee pudding and hints of dried fruits. If this doesn't make you love me, then I taste just as good. An Initial rich toasted fruit bread flavour is superseded by a little chocolate note, with a full yet very clean mouthfeel from my lager fermentation.

beers.name: Jazz Hands
beers.notes: Brewed for the 2026 WC IPA challenge, this year's entry is Jazz hands; The iconic, inspirational, and awesome time-honoured move that's synonymous with the stage. Don't let it be your Mr Cellophane and pass you by at this year's challenge or any other event. Pungent aromas of fresh sticky buds, key lime pie and blackberry crumble layer up into a hop-saturated mouthfeel that jazz's hard. Dry and refined, the bitterness hits early, right with the saturation of flavour and ends the performance perfectly in the West Coast (end) stage, wanting an encore.

beers.name: Cherry Peach
beers.notes:
Brewed in the traditional Belgian way, this wild ale is made from a grist of 40% raw wheat and 60% malted barley,  using a turbid mash, aged hops, and an extended boil. The wort is then cooled overnight in an open coolship,  allowing wild yeasts and bacteria to inoculate it naturally. After spontaneous fermentation, the beer is matured in  oak barrels for at least one year before being refermented on sour cherries and peaches. It is dry hopped with  Mandarina Bavaria prior to packaging. 
From brew day to packaging, the entire process takes around two years. 
Karamu wild ale is ready to enjoy after approximately four months of bottle or keg conditioning. While delicious when  young, it will continue to evolve and drink beautifully for many years.

beers.name: Siege of Liège

Rich and tangy with a slight sweetness, fennel, pear and big oak.

We often work an 80s retro vibe so we named it after the 1988 Tom Hanks comedy. You know, the one with the dodgy plot in which - never mind. 

Anyway, the beer. I think maybe we were thinking it was a one off but it  turned out really good so we kept making it. And making it, and making it. So here we are, it's Beervana ’26, Big is our centrepiece, and it’s bigger. We have a sick Zoltar machine. We have a whole line-up with names referencing the Tom Hanks movie. beers.name: Become the Ocean

Fruity, tart and just a little salty, we think Become the Ocean is the perfect match to a plate of shellfish

beers.name: Vintage Stout 2024 - Pōkeno Whisky Barrel Aged
beers.notes:
The 2024 Vintage Stout is the sixth release of our ‘Vintage’ range of yearly Barrel Aged releases.

This Imperial Stout was brewed with a ‘Reiterated’ Double Mashing schedule, in which the second mash is mixed in with high gravity Wort from the first mash. This process allows us to extract a more concentrated sweet Wort, which feeds the yeast to create a higher alcohol brew.

A small addition of dextrose sugar in the fermenter added an extra hit of alcohol which gives this beer a warming balance to the oak tannins. We then decanted the beer into New Zealand Whisky Barrels from Pōkeno Distillery, and left the beer to rest for nine months.

The process of Oak ageing creates a chemical reaction between the wood and the beer, in which flavour compounds such as tannins and vanillins leach into the beer, creating a rounded and complex flavour. By treating the oak barrel as an additional ‘ingredient’ we’ve been able to create this complex and rich brew that is perfect for winter nights, and will also cellar extremely well as it gains complexity with ageing.

beers.notes: The kind of beer you just can’t stop talking about. Some beers you just drink; this one gets passed along - one sip, a text to a mate, and suddenly everyone is asking where to get it. Chin Wag is a session fruited hazy where the yeast does the talking, turning hops into pure tropical goodness. Built for sharing, oversharing, and spreading gossip. Flavours: A soft pilsner malt base stays clean and muted to keep the fruit honest. White Labs WLP077 Tropicale yeast frees aromatic thiols from a mash charge of NZ Nelson Sauvin and Taiheke, complemented by a high-krausen addition of Citra and a finish of Nectaron. Real mango and passionfruit purée are added cold to lock in a smooth, pillowy body tasting of grapefruit, guava, soft pineapple, and stone fruit.

Big flavour, without the booze so you can enjoy your IPA every day. Tiny, but mighty. NZBA 2025 GOLD MEDAL

beers.name: Your Wish Is Granted
beers.notes: Maybe you didn't know that this is what you wanted. Well no take-backs. Zoltar has searched your soul and determined that instead of world peace or an end to social media disinformation you actually just want a strong hazy with Nelson Sauvin, Motueka and Simcoe. It tastes of grape, lime and tropical fruit. Maybe a little pine too. Mistrusting the soul's true desires is a central theme of Andrei Tarkovsky's 1979 film Stalker, a quiet masterpiece of Soviet-era science fiction and a much better film than Big.
